goal: Give every transfer a durable cross-machine forensic log and a reusable local job definition so operators can inspect, rerun, and retry failed work by job ID without executing it from the wrong machine.
recommended_approach: Build a versioned core job ledger with three linked artifacts: an immutable normalized JobSpec owned by the initiating machine, a RunRecord containing status and retry state, and an append-only EventLog per participant. Mint one run ID at initiation, propagate it through DelegatedPull and SessionOpen with participant, role, and attempt identifiers, emit structured events from the unified transfer pipeline, and persist them through a bounded dedicated writer into crash-recoverable compressed files. Render text and JSON as projections of those events, reconcile detached results from the authoritative daemon, and create a child run from the saved spec plus exact failed-path manifest when retrying.
comparison: The change gets the operator-facing commands, distributed logging, retention, compression, unified run identity, and incremental delivery broadly right. It is not the best approach as written because the durable artifact model is underspecified, detached runs have no mechanism to finalize their initiating-machine record, and crash and multi-participant semantics are unresolved. The guard test resolve_pull_detach_disables_client_hangup passed at head, failed after a deliberate hangup-lifecycle mutation, and passed again after restoration, confirming the detached daemon really outlives the initiating CLI as relied upon here.
material_changes: Separate and version a normalized JobSpec, RunRecord, and per-participant EventLog instead of relying on one loosely defined JSON job format.
Define reconciliation for detached jobs across every local jobs operation, not only jobs retry.
Key logs by run ID plus participant, role, and attempt, and define the structured event schema before implementing storage or retrieval.
Specify partial-log recovery, atomic finalization, pruning concurrency, writer backpressure, and logging-failure behavior; split jl-1 so these invariants are independently testable.

findings.title: Detached runs cannot finalize their initiating-machine record
findings.evidence: docs/plan/JOB_LOGS.md:180 — a local job is defined to contain how its last run ended and its exact failed paths, but lines 185-187 acknowledge that the CLI exits before a detached outcome exists and specify fetching it only during jobs retry; crates/blit-daemon/src/service/core.rs:1430 confirms the daemon continues after that client exits.
findings.predicted_failure: After a detached transfer completes, the initiating machine's record remains pending or lacks failed paths because no process is left to update it; local list, save, and export therefore cannot satisfy jl-3's promise that every run records how it ended.
findings.better_approach: Persist an immutable local JobSpec at submission and a pending RunRecord referencing the authoritative destination daemon, then make every local read, save, export, and retry operation reconcile and atomically cache the terminal daemon result.

findings.title: Saved jobs are not defined reproducibly or safely across upgrades
findings.evidence: docs/plan/JOB_LOGS.md:158 — run records and indefinitely retained saved jobs share one unspecified JSON format, while line 197 describes only source, destination, and options; current TransferArgs retains raw path strings and a path to --files-from at crates/blit-cli/src/cli.rs:210, crates/blit-cli/src/cli.rs:215, and crates/blit-cli/src/cli.rs:348.
findings.predicted_failure: Running a saved mirror or move from another working directory, after the files-from file changes, or after option-schema evolution can select a different tree or become unreadable, potentially copying or deleting the wrong files.
findings.better_approach: Store a schema-versioned semantic JobSpec with the original working directory, lexically resolved local endpoints, typed remote locators, captured files-from contents, transfer-affecting options only, validation rules, and explicit migrations.

findings.title: Post-run compression leaves the most important failure path undefined
findings.evidence: docs/plan/JOB_LOGS.md:211 — events are written to an uncompressed file and compressed only when the run finishes, with no partial-file discovery, startup recovery, interrupted outcome, or atomic finalization contract.
findings.predicted_failure: A daemon crash, power loss, or forced termination leaves an orphan partial log that retention and GetJobLog may not discover, precisely when forensic evidence is most valuable.
findings.better_approach: Write to a deterministic indexed partial artifact, tolerate a torn final event, checkpoint durability, recover and mark interrupted runs at startup, and atomically rename finalized compressed output; retrieval must transparently serve both active partial and finalized logs.

findings.title: A job ID alone is not a sufficient log storage key
findings.evidence: docs/plan/JOB_LOGS.md:190 — each participating machine records its own part under the same job ID, while line 226 defines GetJobLog as returning one log by ID; crates/blit-daemon/src/delegation_gate.rs:334 permits any resolved source when delegation is enabled, allowing one daemon to participate as both delegated destination and served source.
findings.predicted_failure: Self-delegation or colocated CLI and daemon participants can create multiple writers for the same job ID, causing overwrites, interleaved records, or events whose source and destination roles cannot be distinguished.
findings.better_approach: Use the global run ID for correlation but store and retrieve logs by run ID plus stable participant ID, role, and attempt; let jobs log aggregate or select those participant streams explicitly.
